title.narrative: ICLD- Capacitating Local Leaders in Zimbabwe

description.narrative: Bidraget syftar till att främja kvinnors deltagande i lokalpolitiken för att på lång sikt stärka kapaciteten för lokalt styre.

ICLD has applied to Sida for funding of 11 million SEK to carry out the "Capacitating Local Leaders in Zimbabwe" during the period 2019-2021.
The intervention aims at training 28 plus minus newly elected women councillors, 10 elected male councillors as well as 10 selected Council officials, and 2 officials from Ministry of Local Government Public Works and National Housing (MoLG PW&NH). The ICLD will implement the intervention in partnership with Gender Links, Midlands State University and MoLG PW&NH.
The intervention’s total budget is 11 million SEK, which is wholly supported by the Embassy

The overall aim of the project has been to contribute to improving the quality of local governance and to strengthen the capacity of local officials to provide transparent, effective services to their constituencies.
The rationale of the Training Programme is to focus on local political and administrative leaders in Zimbabwe, believing that they have the potential to act as advocates and role models in their communities. The programme is expected to achieve a high involvement of men and women at the local level to enhance gender equality, service delivery and promote democracy in Zimbabwe.
After completion, the participants are expected to be:
- Gender Champions
- Strong, communicative and inclusive leaders
- Skilled project planners and managers.

The programme has been mainly successful at an individual level. Many participants report that they have been empowered to become more communicative and inclusive leaders. A key for this to happen has according to participants been the exchange visits to neighbouring countries as well as to Sweden. These visits have been very inspiring and provided participants with concrete examples on how to lead more effectively. Being part of the programme provided an important network itself for the participants - finding support and inspiration from each other, for example on how to promote and push different aspects of gender equality.
All programme participants have been able to start different development projects in their ward, covering for example areas such as waste management, access to water, access to education, access to health care, etc. In some cases, the implementation of the development projects have strengthened community dialogue and participation and even resulted in some more permanent consultation structures. It has however been a challenge for the participants to be able to finalize the initiated development projects.
Several participants reported that knowledge obtained from trainings and study visits was shared with colleagues that did not participate in the programme, and that transparency and accountability was strengthened in their councils. A follow-up survey carried out by ICLD among the participants, showed that many participants had implemented various measures to enhance transparency in their councils, such as setting up platforms to receive feedback from the community, improving information-sharing practices and implementing systems to reduce fraud and corruption.
One effect from working with local development projects and reaching out to communities was that in some cases the Councils were reaching out to groups that traditionally did not engage with the Councils. One such example came from Makonde RDC, where the Council managed to engage in dialogue with women from the highly religious Marange church when planning for construction of a clinic.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
